issues.description: Template StockIngredient exposes the ingredient quantity via a method named retrieveQuantity(), but other template code (Stock, Main) and the solution expect a getter named getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields", implying a getQuantity() convention. This name mismatch causes compilation errors in the template and will confuse students about which getter to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the getter name for quantity. Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template to getQuantity() (keeping the same return type and behavior) so that Stock, Main, and student code can call getQuantity(). Alternatively, update usages in Stock and Main to call retrieveQuantity(), but the preferred fix is to provide getQuantity() to match the problem statement convention and the solution.

issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class exposes the quantity getter as retrieveQuantity(), while the solution (and the example Main code in the template) use getQuantity(). The problem statement explicitly asks to "add getters for all the private fields", which leads students to expect standard getter names (getQuantity). This mismatch creates confusion and a likely compile/runtime error when Main or student code calls getQuantity() but the template only provides retrieveQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and keep setQuantity as-is) so the getter follows the standard getX naming convention and matches the problem statement, the example Main usage, and the solution implementation.
